newsitem.title: HONG KONG: A Hong Kong's founder statue covered in red paint.
newsitem.headline: A Hong Kong's founder statue covered in red paint.

text.p: A Hong Kong man threw red paint on a statue of one of the colony's founders on Saturday after completion of restoration of a monument to Queen Victoria damaged in an attack four months ago, Hong Kong police said.

Police said they were called to the Statue Square in Hong Kong's Central business district after complaints that Thomas Jackson's bronze figure and a stone lion outside the former Bank of China building were being vandalised.

Police were looking for a Chinese man, who fled the scene after throwing the red paint on one of Hong Kong's colonial symbols, a police spokeswoman said. Damage to the statue was not extensive. Only her shoes were splashed with red paint.
Jackson was the general manager of Hongkong Bank, one of the pillars of the emerging British colony.
Last September, a Chinese artist painted Queen Victoria's statue red and dented her nose. But the statue has been restored to its former glory.

Pun Sing-lui, a 27-year-old artist from mainland China, carried out the attack on the statue in Hong Kong's Victoria Park, saying his action was to protest against "dull, colonial culture", the South China Morning Post said.
Pun was sentenced to 28 days in jail for vandalising the statue of the seated monarch, which is placed at the entrance of one of the British colony's biggest parks.
Pun has since won a HK$60,000 ($7,700) prize from the Philippe Charriol Foundation as "most promising artist" for sculpture, the newspaper said.
The statue's reign in the territory is likely to be cut short, however, despite the HK$150,000 ($19,230) spent on restoring it.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 and all colonial symbols in the territory are likely to be removed.
